70	
71	Write the exploration log to a file from [references/exploration-log-template.md](references/exploration-log-template.md) before the first look; a budget, stop rule, or reservation that first appears in the final report was not precommitted.

73	### Frame
74	
75	State the exploration goal — what a useful lead would look like — and the decision or audience it serves, if any.
76	Pin the dataset, timeframe, and units.
77	Precommit an effort budget (tool calls, queries, or wall-clock — pick one and a number) and a stop rule.
78	Extending either later requires a dated amendment with a reason, never a silent continuation.
79	Decide the confirmation reservation: name the holdout — a later window, an unexamined slice, an independent source — that Explore will not touch, so a handed-off lead has promotion evidence an investigation can use.
80	When no reservation is feasible, record that instead; Handoff must then say that confirmation needs future or independent data.
81	Interactive: pause for user input when judgment calls shaped the framing.
82	Headless: skip the pause, state the assumptions made, and proceed within the gates.
83	
84	### Orient
85	
86	Record the source inventory, schema, grain, and provenance.
87	Run the validity pass: missingness, duplicates, sentinel values.
88	Check coverage at the grain exploration will use against an expected schedule or an independent denominator; when neither exists, record coverage as unverifiable rather than clean.
89	For any source whose absent records could bear on a lead, record what absence means — event absent, event unrecorded, or export incomplete — and when no evidence discriminates those readings, record the semantics as `UNKNOWN`; a source's own missingness pattern can never establish its own completeness.
90	Record known instrument caveats.
91	No pattern interpretation before the orientation record exists: quality artifacts masquerade as findings, and a pattern noticed early is quarantined as unvalidated until Orient completes.
92	
93	### Explore
94	
95	A look is one output examined during Explore — a query result, a table, a plot, a matrix you actually read; Orient's examinations belong to the orientation record, not the register.
96	Every look gets a register line: family, what was examined, and roughly how many comparisons the output exposed (a correlation matrix over ten variables is one look exposing forty-five pairs).
97	Inspect a variable's distribution before leaning on scalar summaries of it — a mean or a correlation over a distribution you have not seen is a guess wearing a number.
98	When a look changes the analytic population — a join, a filter, an aggregation, a new denominator — revalidate grain, join cardinality, and coverage at the new population before its output can seed a lead candidate; Orient checked the data you were given, not the data you just made.
99	A surprising pattern becomes a lead candidate, never a finding.
100	Chasing a candidate is allowed within budget; the chase's looks are register entries like any others, and the reserved evidence stays untouched.
101	Data-quality anomalies discovered here are first-class lead candidates, not obstacles to route around.
102	No invented confidence numbers; when a formal multiplicity correction would matter, that is confirmation work — hand off.
103	
104	### Consolidate
105	
106	Dedupe candidates and rank the survivors.
107	Search context has consequences, not just a record.
108	Between two leads of the same class whose magnitudes do not clearly separate, the one whose search context exposed fewer comparisons ranks higher.
109	A magnitude selected by search is reported as likely overstated, with the honest estimate deferred to the confirming test.
110	Each reported lead records: a statement in associational wording, its class (`pattern`, `data-quality`, or `descriptive`), an evidence pointer, its search context (how many looks, across how many families, exposing roughly how many comparisons), the plausible alternative explanations noted but not tested, the cheapest adequate confirming test, and a disposition (`reported`, `handed-off`, or `dropped`).

114	
115	Leads the user wants settled go to `hypothesis-driven-analysis` and enter as `retrospective` hypotheses.

117	This skill's outputs are only: leads, descriptive facts the records settle, and data-quality issues.
118	No causal assertions anywhere: exploration never asserts or implies that one thing caused another, because nothing in an open-ended search identifies a cause.

122	
123	Frame-lite is the scope pin and the budget only — profiling seeks orientation, not leads, so it takes no lead-shaped goal and no reservation.

137

139	- Minimize collection.

142	
143	## Degraded Modes
144	
145	- No file tools: emit Frame — budget, stop rule, reservation — or, on the profile route, Frame-lite as § Profile Route defines it, as response text before any exploration output, and record that the precommitment is then only as strong as the visible message order.

147	- Unauthorized or unreachable sources: explore the authorized subset and report the rest as needing authorization, per the gate.
148	
149	## Record Delivery
150	
151	<!-- shared: record-delivery -->
152	Before delivering a conclusion, report, or handoff backed by a full investigation ledger, exploration log, identification review, decision record, or VoI record that you wrote or updated as a file, run the plugin's structural validator in its completed-record mode against the record's final saved contents: `python3 "<plugin-root>/instruments/check_record.py" --final "<record-path>"`, where `<plugin-root>` is the directory two levels above this SKILL.md, resolved through any symlink.

154	Never change a number, a provenance class, or a sentinel only to clear a finding: a sentinel belongs to the verdict the skill assigns it to, and a finding you cannot fix on the skill's terms is a limitation to report, not a line to rewrite.
155	A clean result is structural evidence only, never a claim that the analysis is right.
156	When the validator, `python3`, or the ability to run a command is unavailable, report the record as not validated and name the reason; install nothing and claim no clean pass.
157	Mini ledgers, estimation records, and collection plans carry no validator signature and owe no run.
158	<!-- /shared: record-delivery -->
159	
160	## Non-Goals
161	
162	- Adjudicating claims, explaining named effects, or estimating quantities under uncertainty — an investigation's work, wherever it lives.
163	- Direct retrieval and bounded descriptive queries — answer those directly with no ceremony.
164	- Prose-document summarization.
165	- Teaching statistical or visualization technique: this skill enforces process discipline; co-loaded skills and the agent's own competence carry the methods.

| id | Origin (file, query, system) | Acquired | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
